title: See what kinds of files are in there
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

extension-map-covers-real-drive-bytes: C: Other = 50.2% of 767 GB on-disk (limit 25%); no-extension 17.6%, .aax 9.0% (limit 5%)
installers-identifiable-by-name-alone: Name rule matched 6.5% of Downloads installer bytes (2 of 8 files); needs 70%

PS-005 names 'installers' as a kind, but a name rule found only 6.5% of Downloads installer bytes. Does the person accept an Installers row limited to package formats (.msi, .msp, .msu, .msix, .appx and bundles), with setup programs shipped as .exe counted under 'Programs & system files' and a tooltip saying so? Default in this design: yes. The alternative is a location rule (for example, any .exe under Downloads is an installer), which needs an ancestor lookup per file.

Installers as package formats only (msi/msix/appx) with every .exe under Programs, against a location heuristic (.exe in Downloads) or a broader name rule. Measured evidence favours the narrow row, but the label is a product choice.
No-extension as its own row, against folding it into Other. A dotfile such as .gitignore falls into Other under the current rule, not no-extension.
Dropping ts from Videos (avoids TypeScript inflation on a dev machine) against keeping it (MPEG transport streams on a media machine).
Ten fixed kinds, with sys folded into 'Programs & system files', against separate Programs and System rows.
Top 3 extensions inline per row, against a drill-down list or a per-extension table like FolderSizes' File Types report. This slice ships no drill-down.
Compute once synchronously on the UI thread at scan end, against Task.Run. About 150-190 ms at 5M records was accepted.
The report carries per-kind totals only. Extension detail in the report would help debugging but puts name fragments in a diagnostic file.
Where the kind table and enum live: Core/Analysis beside LargestFiles, against a separate Core/Kinds folder.
